newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santista confirms Incobrasa deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santista confirms Incobrasa deal.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Santista Alimentos has bought Incobrasa's soybean processing and warehousing facilities in the key growing state of Rio Grande do Sul, the company confirmed in a statement.
The deal, leaked in Brazilian newspapers last week, was valued at $80 million according to traders although the company declined to put a value on the purchase.

Santista, a subsidiary of Bunge y Born, said the deal included two soybean processing plants with a combined capacity for crushing 5,700 tonnes per day, three warehouses and Incobrasa's terminal at the southern port of Rio Grande.

"The operation consolidates Santista as one of the leaders in the national soybean and soy product market, with a capacity for processing around 3.6 million tonnes per year in its six industrial crushing units," Santista said in the press release.
Incobrasa's revenue was close to 300 million reais ($286 million) in 1996, Santista said.
Santista director Ruy Hirschheimer said the production of the two new crushing plants would be entirely exported.
"With this acquisition, our exports should reach close to $600 million per year, double the volume shipped in 1996," Hirschheimer said in the statement.
Santista owns 29 industrial units and employs 8,700 people. Revenues were 2.15 billion reais in 1996 with a net profit of 46 million reais, up 109 percent on the previous year.

Since late 1995, Santista has concentrated its investments in the wheat and soybeans sectors. The company expects to invest 450 million reais over the next three years to expand capacity and build new units. This amount excludes new acquisitions.
